verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and our brother Timothy,
to God's holy and faithful people in Christ at Colossae: Grace and peace to you from God our Father.
We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you,
because we've heard about your faith in Christ Jesus and the love you have for all God's people.
Your faith and love come from the hope stored up for you in heaven. You heard about this hope earlier in the true message of the Good News,
which has reached you. Just as it is bearing fruit and growing throughout the world, it has been doing the same among you since the day you heard it and truly understood God's grace.
You learned this from Epaphras, our dear fellow servant, who is a faithful servant of Christ on your behalf.
He also told us about the love the Spirit has given you.
That's why, from the day we heard about you, we haven't stopped praying for you. We ask God to fill you with the knowledge of his will through all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
so you can live in a way worthy of the Lord and please him in every way: producing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God.
May you be strengthened with all power according to his glorious might, so you can endure everything with patience and joy,
and give thanks to the Father, who has qualified you to share in the inheritance of his people in the light.
He rescued us from the power of darkness and brought us into the Kingdom of his beloved Son.
In the Son we have redemption—the forgiveness of sins.
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation.
Everything in heaven and on earth was created through him, visible and invisible—thrones, powers, rulers, and authorities. Everything was created through him and for him.
He existed before everything, and everything holds together in him.
He is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning and the firstborn from the dead, so that he might be first in everything.
God was pleased to have all his fullness live in him,
and through him to reconcile everything to himself, making peace through the blood of his cross for everything on earth and in heaven.
At one time you were separated from God and hostile toward him in your thinking, shown by the evil things you did.
But now Christ has reconciled you through his physical body and death, to present you holy, blameless, and beyond accusation before God—

if you continue in the faith, firmly grounded and steady, without shifting away from the hope in the Good News you heard. This Good News has been announced to every creature under heaven, and I, Paul, became its servant.
Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you. In my body, I complete what remains of Christ's afflictions for the sake of his body, the church.
I became its servant through the responsibility God gave me for you: to make God's message fully known,
the mystery hidden for ages and generations but now revealed to God's people.
God wanted to make known to them the glorious riches of this mystery among the Gentiles: Christ in you, the hope of glory.
We proclaim Christ, warning and teaching everyone with all wisdom, so we can present everyone mature in Christ.
That's why I work so hard, struggling with all the energy Christ powerfully works in me.
I want you to know how hard I'm working for you, for the believers in Laodicea, and for everyone who hasn't met me face to face.
My goal is for them to be encouraged and united in love, and to enjoy the full confidence that comes from understanding, so they can know God's mystery—Christ himself.
All the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Christ.
I'm telling you this so no one can mislead you with clever arguments.
Though I'm away in body, I'm with you in spirit, and I'm glad to see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
So then, just as you received Christ Jesus as Lord, keep living your lives in him.
Stay rooted and built up in him, firm in the faith you were taught, and overflowing with gratitude.
Watch out that no one captures you with empty, deceptive philosophy based on human traditions and the principles of this world rather than on Christ.
All the fullness of God lives in Christ in bodily form,
and you have been brought to fullness in him. He is the head over every ruler and authority.
In him you were also circumcised—not by human hands, but by putting off the sinful nature, through the circumcision done by Christ.
You were buried with Christ in baptism, and raised with him through faith in God's power, the God who raised him from the dead.
You were dead in your trespasses and in your uncircumcised human nature, but God made you alive with Christ and forgave all our trespasses.
He erased the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. He took it away by nailing it to the cross.
He disarmed rulers and authorities and exposed them publicly, triumphing over them through the cross.
So don't let anyone judge you about what you eat or drink, or about a festival, a new moon, or a Sabbath.
These are only shadows of what was coming; the reality is found in Christ.
Don't let anyone disqualify you by insisting on false humility and the worship of angels. Such people go on about visions they've supposedly seen and become arrogant for no reason.
They aren't holding on to Christ, the head. From him the whole body is nourished and held together by its joints and ligaments, and it grows as God makes it grow.
Since you died with Christ to the principles of this world, why do you submit to its rules as if you still belonged to it?
‘Don't handle! Don't taste! Don't touch!’
These rules are about things that disappear with use. They're based on human commands and teachings.
Such rules look wise because of their self-made worship, false humility, and harsh treatment of the body, but they don't restrain the desires of our human nature.
Since you were raised with Christ, focus on the things above, where Christ is seated at God's right hand.
Set your minds on what is above, not on earthly things.
You died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, who is your life, appears, you'll also appear with him in glory.
So put to death whatever belongs to your earthly nature: sexual immorality, impurity, uncontrolled passion, evil desire, and greed, which is idolatry.
Because of these things, God's anger is coming on those who disobey.
You used to live that way too, when you were part of that life.
But now get rid of all of it: anger, rage, malice, slander, and obscene talk.
Don't lie to one another. You've taken off the old self and its practices,
and put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge to become like its Creator.
In this new life there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, foreigner, Scythian, enslaved or free. Christ is everything and is in everyone.
So as God's chosen, holy, and dearly loved people, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
Put up with one another and forgive each other whenever someone has a complaint. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
Above all, put on love, which ties everything together in perfect unity.
Let Christ's peace rule in your hearts, since you were called to peace as one body. And be thankful.
Let Christ's word live richly among you. Teach and guide one another with all wisdom, through psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Sing to God with gratitude in your hearts.
Whatever you do, in word or action, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting for those who belong to the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives, and don't treat them harshly.
Children, obey your parents in everything, because this pleases the Lord.
Fathers, don't discourage your children, or they'll lose heart.
Enslaved people, obey your earthly masters in everything. Don't work only when they're watching, just to please them; work sincerely, out of reverence for the Lord.
Whatever you do, work at it wholeheartedly, as if you were working for the Lord, not for people.
You know that the Lord will reward you with the inheritance. You serve the Lord Christ.
Anyone who does wrong will be repaid for the wrong they did, and God shows no favoritism.
Masters, treat your enslaved workers justly and fairly. Remember that you also have a Master in heaven.
Keep praying faithfully. Stay alert, and give thanks.
At the same time, pray for us too, that God will open a door for our message so we can share the mystery of Christ, for which I'm in chains.
Pray that I'll make it clear, as I should.
Be wise in the way you act toward outsiders, making the most of every opportunity.
Let your words always be gracious and thoughtful, so you'll know how to answer each person.
Tychicus, our dear brother, faithful servant, and fellow worker in the Lord, will tell you everything about me.
I sent him for this very reason: so you can know how we're doing, and so he can encourage your hearts.
Onesimus is coming with him. He's a faithful and dearly loved brother, one of your own. They'll tell you everything that's happening here.
Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, sends greetings, as does Mark, Barnabas' cousin. You've received instructions about him: welcome him if he comes to you.
Jesus, who is called Justus, sends greetings too. These are the only fellow workers for God's Kingdom from the circumcised group who have been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, one of your own and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, asking that you'll stand firm, mature, and fully confident in everything God wants.
I can testify that he works hard for you, and for the believers in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
Luke, our dear doctor, and Demas send greetings.
Give my greetings to the brothers and sisters in Laodicea, and to Nympha and the church that meets in her home.
After this letter has been read among you, make sure it's read in the church in Laodicea too. And you should read the letter from Laodicea.
Tell Archippus, ‘Pay attention to the ministry you received in the Lord, and carry it out.’
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember that I'm in chains. Grace be with you. Amen.
